events.description: The cook checks pans of roasted banana pieces in the open oven, then moves to the kitchen island to prepare the blender.
Using a red spatula, the cook repeatedly scoops browned banana pieces from a dark baking dish into the blender pitcher.
The emptied baking dish is carried back to the stove area, and the cook returns to the open oven.
The cook removes a hot loaf pan from the oven with a towel and scrapes a second batch of roasted bananas into the blender pitcher; one piece falls onto the counter.
The empty loaf pan is set down and carried toward the sink before the cook returns to the island with the filled blender pitcher.
The blender pitcher is placed on a Vitamix base, covered with its lid and cap, and connected for use.
The cook holds the blender lid and repeatedly adjusts the controls, blending the roasted bananas into a thick brown puree.
The cook opens the countertop ice-cream maker and handles its lid, freezer bowl, and paddle in preparation for filling it.
A lemon half is squeezed with a handheld citrus press, adding juice to the banana puree in the blender pitcher.
The cook stirs the lemon juice into the puree with the red spatula and replaces the blender lid.
The puree is blended again briefly, then uncovered and stirred while the cook checks its smooth consistency.
A small dog walks across the kitchen floor near the cook's work area.
The cook carries the finished puree from the blender station toward the ice-cream maker.
The cook pours the banana puree into the ice-cream maker's freezer bowl and repeatedly scrapes the blender pitcher to transfer the remaining mixture.
The ice-cream maker is repositioned on the island and its power cord is routed across the kitchen and connected.
The cook presses the ice-cream maker controls several times, changing the displayed timer setting.
The clear lid is removed, and the cook lifts and reseats the filled freezer bowl and paddle before restarting the machine.
The ice-cream maker churns the brown mixture while the cook monitors it, makes occasional lid and paddle adjustments, and ultimately leaves the clear lid in place.
While the machine continues running, the cook looks down and reads the open recipe book beside the milk, lemon, and utensils.

events.description: The cook surveys the crowded stovetop workspace and reaches for a small paring knife.
The cook peels several onions with the paring knife, dropping skins and scraps into a lined bin beside the stove.
The peeled onions are placed on a cutting board and repeatedly sliced and diced with a chef's knife.
The cook turns a stove control, activating a burner for the large pot.
The cook opens the refrigerator and retrieves a jar containing solid white cooking fat.
Several spoonfuls of the white cooking fat are scraped from the jar into the large pot.
The cutting board is tipped over the pot to transfer the first batch of diced onions into the heated fat.
The cook returns to the scrap bin and peels another onion with the paring knife.
The additional peeled onion is sliced and diced on the cutting board.
The second batch of chopped onion is added to the pot and stirred into the cooking mixture.
The cook opens the refrigerator, retrieves a produce bag containing green peppers, and brings it to the stove.
Green peppers are trimmed, split lengthwise, cleaned of seeds and inner ribs over the scrap bin, then sliced and diced on the board.
The chopped green pepper is transferred from the cutting board into the steaming onion pot and stirred in.
The cook opens a zip-top bag of pale prepared pieces and adds some of its contents to the pot.
The cook selects seasonings from the cabinet and spice area, shakes one bottled seasoning and then a brown powdered seasoning into the steaming pot.
A small saucepan is lifted and its cooked contents are poured into the large pot while the mixture is stirred.
The combined mixture is stirred and left to simmer vigorously in the large pot as heavy steam rises.

events.description: The visitor passes a decorated Christmas tree and approaches a brightly lit wall display of historic firearms.
The visitor slowly examines a wall case containing mounted long guns, open presentation cases, photographs, labels, and a large curved tusk.
The visitor backs away from the wall case and moves past an information kiosk toward a freestanding display.
The visitor studies a sloped glass cabinet filled with antique pistols and accessories arranged in ornate fitted cases.
The visitor turns across the gallery and relocates to an adjacent freestanding cabinet.
The visitor examines another illuminated cabinet containing cased revolvers, loose long-barreled handguns, ammunition, and a small coffin-shaped pistol case.
The visitor inspects a neighboring cabinet holding a long gun in a metal case, several green and gray pistol cases, loose mechanical parts, photographs, and labels.
The visitor pauses at a separate display featuring gold-accented firearms, long barrels, presentation pieces, and a historical photograph.
The visitor walks around and examines an Olympiad-themed glass enclosure containing mounted rifles and pistols, documents, a digital panel, and a tan blazer on a mannequin.
The visitor turns back through the gallery toward a tall glass rack densely filled with long guns.
The visitor examines rows of rifles and shotguns mounted inside the tall glass rack, including open presentation cases along its base.
The visitor moves across the gallery past central cabinets and the Christmas tree toward a wall display labeled “Holland & Holland.”
The visitor closely surveys the Holland & Holland wall case, viewing mounted long guns and numerous open presentation cases with firearms, ammunition, photographs, and documents.
The visitor leaves the wall case and approaches a large central glass island displaying handguns.
The visitor circles and studies the central handgun display, first viewing cased revolvers on the lower shelf and then rows of pistols and revolvers on the raised upper shelf.
The visitor turns away from the handgun island and surveys the adjacent gallery and wall-mounted firearm displays.
